state_body: Office of Renewable Energy Siting and Electric Transmission (ORES), Department of Public Service
summary: Renewable facilities of 25 MW or more (with co-located storage) need an ORES siting permit under Public Service Law Article VIII; facilities of 20 to 25 MW may opt in, and smaller facilities stay under municipal zoning. Stand-alone battery storage is outside the ORES rules.
amendments_note: Superseded since the inventory: the inventory cites N.Y. Executive Law § 94-c, which nysenate.gov no longer lists ('requested entry could not be found'); the program now sits in Public Service Law Article VIII (§§ 136-148), shown on nysenate.gov as last revised 2024-06-21 (the 2024 RAPID Act; session-law chapter not confirmed from the statute pages). ORES rules moved to 16 NYCRR Part 1100, effective 2024-07-17. Later amendments not checked.
draft_note: Read 2026-10-09 via WebFetch (curl got a Cloudflare challenge, HTTP 403): https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/PBS/A8 (section list), /PBS/137 (definition 4: 'twenty-five thousand kilowatts or more' plus co-located storage), /PBS/140 (siting permit required). WebFetch returns short exact quotes through a summarizer, so a reviewer may want to re-open. The 20 to 25 MW opt-in was not found in the statute pages read; it appears in 16 NYCRR 1100-1.2(ba), and 1100-1.1(b)(5) excludes stand-alone battery storage. Rule read in full from https://dps.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2024/08/chapter-xi-title-16-of-nycrr-part-1100-generation-siting-effective-2024-07-17.pdf.
review_note: Read 2026-10-09: N.Y. Pub. Serv. Law 137 and 140 via WebFetch of https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/PBS/137 and /PBS/140 (curl and Jina Reader got the Cloudflare challenge, HTTP 403); WebFetch quoted 137(4) 'nameplate generating capacity of twenty-five thousand kilowatts or more' with 'any co-located system storing energy', and 140(1) requiring a siting permit; both pages show most recent revision 2024-06-21. Also read the new ORES rules on dps.ny.gov: 16 NYCRR Part 1100 General Procedures (https://dps.ny.gov/chapter-xi-title-16-nycrr-part-1100-general-procedures) and Part 1101 (https://dps.ny.gov/chapter-xi-title-16-nycrr-part-1101-major-renewable-energy-facility-siting), and the redline comparing Part 1100 to the 2024-07-17 version. The 25 MW threshold, the storage treatment and hybrid are right. Disagreements: (1) summary: 'facilities of 20 to 25 MW may opt in' is no longer true. https://dps.ny.gov/ores-regulatory-documents and /ores-overview say new Parts 1100, 1101 and 1102 'became effective as of March 9, 2026', replacing the Part 1100 of 2024-07-17. The new Part 1100 has no opt-in definition (the redline strikes former 1100-1.2(ba) 'Opt-in renewable energy facility' and the opt-in transfer section), and neither 137 nor 140 provides one. (2) statute_citation: 16 NYCRR 1100-1.1(b)(4)-(5), 1100-1.2(ag), (ba) are superseded; the major facility definition is now 1100-1.2(bb) and the storage exclusion is 1100-1.1(d)(5) ('any battery energy storage system not co-located with a major renewable energy facility'). (3) amendments_note: says 'Later amendments not checked'; it must record the 2026-03-09 replacement rules.

state_body: Office of Renewable Energy Siting and Electric Transmission (ORES), Department of Public Service
summary: ORES rules set uniform setbacks for facilities it permits: wind turbines 2.0 times total height from non-participating residences and 1.1 times from property lines and public roads; solar 250 feet from non-participating occupied residences and 100 feet from non-participating residential property lines. Noise is capped at 45 dBA Leq (8-hour) outside non-participating residences.
amendments_note: Part 1100 version effective 2024-07-17 (replacing 19 NYCRR Part 900 after ORES moved to DPS). Amendments after that date not checked.
draft_note: Read the PDF of 16 NYCRR Part 1100 (effective 2024-07-17) from dps.ny.gov. Table 1 also: substations and bulk electric system lines 1.5x, non-participating non-residential structures 1.5x, gas wells 1.1x; manufacturer setbacks apply if stricter. Table 2 also: 50 feet from centerline of public roads and from non-participating non-residential property lines. Noise: 55 dBA at participating residences, 40 dBA Leq (1-hour) from substation equipment. These are application design standards ORES can vary in a permit; the reviewer should decide whether they count as a statewide standard.
review_note: Read 2026-10-09 the PDF at statute_url (16 NYCRR Part 1100 effective 2024-07-17) and the current rules: 16 NYCRR Part 1101, effective 2026-03-09 (https://dps.ny.gov/chapter-xi-title-16-nycrr-part-1101-major-renewable-energy-facility-siting), with https://dps.ny.gov/ores-regulatory-documents stating the new Parts 1100, 1101 and 1102 took effect March 9, 2026 and the 2024 Part 1100 is now 'Former'. The distances still match: new 1101-2.5(b) Table 5-1 (wind: 2 times total height from non-participating residences, 1.1 times from property lines and public roads) and 1101-2.5(d) Table 5-2 (solar: 250 feet from non-participating occupied residences, 100 feet from non-participating residential property lines). Disagreements: (1) summary: noise is now 45 dBA Leq (2-hour) outside non-participating type 1 receptors for wind (1101-3.5(a)(1)(i)) and 45 dBA Leq (1-hour) for solar (1101-2.7(b)(2)), not '45 dBA Leq (8-hour)', which was the superseded 1100-2.8(b). (2) statute_citation and statute_url: 16 NYCRR 1100-2.6(b), 1100-2.6(d) and 1100-2.8(b) and the 2024 PDF are superseded; the current provisions are 1101-2.5(b) Table 5-1, 1101-2.5(d) Table 5-2, 1101-2.7(b) and 1101-3.5(a). (3) amendments_note: 'Amendments after that date not checked' misses the 2026-03-09 replacement.

summary: A board of county commissioners may designate all or part of the county's unincorporated area as a restricted area that bars large solar facilities and wind farms of 5 MW or more, and the Power Siting Board may not accept applications there; the county may also prohibit or shrink an individual project within 90 days after the developer's required public meeting.
amendments_note: 303.58 amended by 2024 Ohio HB 497 (135th GA), eff. 2025-04-09, adding newspaper, state public notice website or county website and social media as notice methods. 303.57, 303.59 to 303.62, 4906.021 and 4906.022 show only the SB 52 enactment (eff. 2021-10-11) in their version history on codes.ohio.gov as of 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read on codes.ohio.gov: 303.57 (definitions; battery additions are not material amendments), 303.58 (restricted area resolution, notice to school districts, municipalities and boards of township trustees, map filed with recorder), 303.59 (effective in 30 days unless 8 percent of county gubernatorial vote petitions for a referendum), 303.60 (Board may not accept applications in a restricted area), 303.61 (developer public meeting 90 to 300 days before applying, notice to county and townships), 303.62 (county may prohibit or limit boundaries within 90 days; silence lets the application proceed), 4906.021 and 4906.022. Township provisions: townships get notice and a voting ad hoc seat on the Board (township trustee chair or designee) but no veto or restricted-area power; chapter 519 index has no SB 52 section. Solar threshold is via 'large solar facility' (a major utility facility, 50 MW or more). SB 52 uncodified grandfather clauses not read (legislature.ohio.gov failed TLS verification through the proxy on 2026-10-09).
review_note: Read on codes.ohio.gov 2026-10-09: sections 303.57, 303.58, 303.59, 303.60, 303.61, 303.62, 4906.021 and 4906.022 (https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-303.58 and the matching pages). 303.58(A): the board of county commissioners may designate all or part of the unincorporated area as a restricted area prohibiting economically significant wind farms (5 to under 50 MW), large wind farms and large solar facilities (50 MW or more). 303.60: no person may file and the Power Siting Board may not accept an application in a restricted area. 303.61: developer public meeting 90 to 300 days before applying. 303.62: within 90 days after that meeting the county may prohibit the facility or limit its boundaries; with no resolution the application proceeds. 303.59 adds a referendum on petition by 8 percent of the county gubernatorial vote. Summary, thresholds solar:50 and wind:5, and local_government match. Amendments confirmed: 303.58 amended by HB 497 (135th GA) eff. 2025-04-09 (notice by newspaper, state public notice website, or county website and social media); the other sections show only the SB 52 enactment eff. 2021-10-11.

summary: No political subdivision may require any approval, permit or other condition for a major utility facility or economically significant wind farm holding a Board certificate, apart from local rules unrelated to location, design or pollution control.
amendments_note: Last amended by HB 6 (133rd GA), eff. 2019-10-22; no later version on codes.ohio.gov as of 2026-10-09. Counties' SB 52 powers act before certification (see OH-local_opt_out-1).
draft_note: Read https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.13.
review_note: Read https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.13 on 2026-10-09. 4906.13(B): 'No public agency or political subdivision of this state may require any approval, consent, permit, certificate, or other condition for the construction or operation of a major utility facility or economically significant wind farm authorized by a certificate', saving state employee-protection laws and 'municipal regulations that do not pertain to the location or design of, or pollution control and abatement standards for' the facility. Summary, state body and thresholds (solar:50 via 4906.01(B)(1)(a), wind:5 via 4906.13(A)) match. Version list: last amended by HB 6 (133rd GA) eff. 2019-10-22; no later version as of 2026-10-09.

summary: The Power Siting Board certificates generating plants of 50 MW or more and wind farms of 5 to 50 MW; county and township zoning governs smaller solar and wind, and counties hold a separate veto under SB 52 (see OH-local_opt_out-1).
amendments_note: 4906.01 and 4906.10 amended by 2025 Ohio HB 15 (136th GA), eff. 2025-08-14: 4906.10(D) now requires a Board decision within 150 days after an application is complete or it is deemed approved; HB 15 also added advanced transmission technology language. 303.213 and 519.213 last amended by HB 501 (134th GA), eff. 2023-04-06. 4906.13 last amended 2019 (HB 6); 4906.20 last amended 2014 (HB 483).
draft_note: Read on codes.ohio.gov 2026-10-09: sections 4906.01, 4906.10 (and its 2021 authenticated PDF to compare), 4906.13, 4906.20, 303.213, 519.213. Economically significant wind farm excludes farms operating on 2008-06-24 and single-customer wind under 20 MW (4906.13(A)). Storage is not named in the threshold sections.
review_note: Read on codes.ohio.gov 2026-10-09: sections 4906.01, 4906.10, 4906.13, 4906.20, 303.213 and 519.213 (https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.01 and the matching section pages). 4906.01(B)(1)(a): major utility facility is a generating plant of 'fifty megawatts or more'; (G) and (H) define large solar facility and large wind farm as such plants. 4906.13(A): economically significant wind farm is 'five or more megawatts but less than fifty megawatts'; 4906.20(A) requires a Board certificate for it. 303.213 and 519.213: county and township zoning covers small wind farms (outside Board jurisdiction) and small solar facilities under 50 MW. SB 52 county powers are in 303.57 to 303.62 (read for OH-local_opt_out-1). Thresholds solar:50, wind:5 and hybrid match. Amendments confirmed from the version lists: 4906.01 and 4906.10 amended by HB 15 (136th GA) eff. 2025-08-14, and 4906.10(D) now reads that the Board decides within 150 days after the application is complete or it is deemed approved; 303.213 and 519.213 last amended by HB 501 eff. 2023-04-06; 4906.13 last amended by HB 6 eff. 2019-10-22; 4906.20 by HB 483 eff. 2014-09-15. Nothing later shown.

summary: Turbines in Board-certificated wind farms must be at least 1.1 times total height from the wind farm property line and at least 1,125 feet from the blade tip to the nearest adjacent property line, unless all adjacent owners waive it.
amendments_note: Both sections last amended by 2014 Ohio HB 483 (130th GA), eff. 2014-09-15; no later version on codes.ohio.gov as of 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read 4906.20 and 4906.201 on codes.ohio.gov. 4906.201 applies the same setback to wind plants of 50 MW or more. Applications found compliant before 2013-09-29 keep a 750-foot distance. The statute directs the Board to set this minimum by rule (Ohio Adm. Code chapter 4906-4, not read).
review_note: Read https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-4906.20 and section-4906.201 on 2026-10-09. 4906.20(B)(2)(a): Board rules must set a minimum turbine setback of 1.1 times total height (base to tip of highest blade) from the wind farm property line and at least 1,125 feet from the tip of the nearest blade at ninety degrees to the property line of the nearest adjacent property; (c): applies unless all adjacent owners waive it, or the Board requires more; (b)(i) keeps 750 feet for applications found compliant before 2013-09-29. 4906.201 applies the same setback to wind plants of 50 MW or more. Summary, wind:5 threshold and state_board match. Both sections show only the HB 483 (130th GA) version eff. 2014-09-15; no later version as of 2026-10-09.

summary: Oklahoma has no state siting permit for wind or solar; the Corporation Commission takes notices and reports and enforces statutory wind setbacks, while any land use approval comes from county or municipal zoning where it exists.
statute_citation: Okla. Stat. tit. 17, §§ 160.11-160.23 (Oklahoma Wind Energy Development Act)
amendments_note: 160.21 has a 2023 version (SB 782, Laws 2023, c. 126, § 22). 2025-2026 wind setback bills HB 2751 (failed in Senate Energy committee) and SB 2 (failed on House reading) were not enacted per oklegislature.gov bill pages checked 2026-10-09. Title 17 PDF compiled 2025-12-31.
draft_note: Read the official Title 17 compilation PDF from oklegislature.gov (OSCN DeliverDocument pages return a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge and WebFetch got HTTP 403). 160.21 requires notice to the Commission and county commissioners and a public meeting; 160.22 lets the Commission adopt rules and fees; no section requires a state siting approval. County zoning statutes (Okla. Stat. tit. 19, § 863.x, cited by the inventory) not read.
review_note: Read the official Title 17 compilation PDF https://oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os17.pdf (created 2025-12-31) on 2026-10-09: the Oklahoma Wind Energy Development Act, 160.11 to 160.23, in full. 160.21 (both versions; v2 is SB 782, Laws 2023, c. 126, s. 22) requires notice of intent to the Corporation Commission, copies to county commissioners and municipalities, newspaper publication and a public meeting before construction; 160.20 sets setbacks the Commission enforces through attestations and penalties; 160.22 gives rulemaking and fee authority. No section requires a state siting approval. Title 17 also has only a Commercial Solar Facility Decommissioning Act (820 et seq.) for solar, which is a lease decommissioning law, not a siting permit. Summary, technology and local_government fit. The statement that land use approval comes from county or municipal zoning rests on the absence of a state permit; the county zoning statutes (tit. 19) were not read by me either. Amendments: oklegislature.gov bill pages checked 2026-10-09 show HB 2751 'Failed in Committee - Energy' and SB 2 'Third Reading, Measure failed: Ayes 44 Nays 49' and, in 2026, 'Fourth Reading, Measure failed: Ayes 20 Nays 67'; neither was enacted.

summary: No wind energy facility tower may be built within 1.5 nautical miles of a public-use or municipal airport runway centerline, a public school or a hospital; separately, each turbine needing an FAA Form 7460-1 needs an FAA no-hazard determination and Defense Department clearance before construction.
amendments_note: History note: added Laws 2015, c. 92; amended Laws 2017, c. 45; Laws 2018, c. 4; Laws 2019, c. 310 (HB 2118, emerg. eff. 2019-05-07); Laws 2023, c. 126, § 21 (eff. 2023-11-01). No 2025-2026 change (HB 2751 and SB 2 not enacted).
draft_note: Read 160.20 in the Title 17 PDF (compiled 2025-12-31) and the enrolled HB 2118 (2019) PDF at https://www.oklegislature.gov/cf_pdf/2019-20%20ENR/hB/HB2118%20ENR.PDF. The distance is nautical miles, measured from the tower base; it applies after 2015-08-21. Subsection C (military clearance) is a clearance requirement, not a distance setback. Disputes go to district court; Commission penalty up to $1,500 per day for failing to file the no-hazard documents.
review_note: Read Okla. Stat. tit. 17, 160.20 in https://oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os17.pdf (created 2025-12-31) on 2026-10-09. 160.20(A): after 2015-08-21 no wind energy facility may be built with any tower base less than 1 1/2 nautical miles from the runway centerline of a public-use airport or a municipally owned airport, from a public school in a public school district, or from a hospital. (C): each turbine or structure needing an FAA Form 7460-1 needs an active FAA Determination of No Hazard and resolution of Defense Department impacts documented by the Clearinghouse before construction. (D): penalty up to $1,500 per day. Summary, technology and state body match. History note matches the amendments_note: added Laws 2015, c. 92; amended 2017 c. 45, 2018 c. 4, 2019 c. 310, 2023 c. 126, s. 21 (eff. 2023-11-01). The 2025-2026 setback bills HB 2751 and SB 2 failed per their oklegislature.gov bill pages (SB 2 also failed a 2026 fourth reading, 20 to 67).

summary: A Council site certificate binds all counties and cities as to site approval, and they must then issue the permits it addresses without further hearings; the Council may also find land use compliance despite unmet local criteria by taking a goal exception.
amendments_note: 469.401 history ends with 2025 c.305. 469.504 amended by 2026 Or. Laws c.46 (HB 4076), which adds a goal-exception finding for facilities using an existing plant's surplus interconnection.
draft_note: Read 469.401 in ORS chapter 469 (2025 edition) and the enrolled 2026 HB 4076. 469.401(5) keeps local authority over matters not in the certificate (building codes, fees).
review_note: Read ORS 469.401 and 469.504 in https://www.oregonlegislature.gov/bills_laws/ors/ors469.html (2025 edition) and enrolled 2026 HB 4076 (https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2026R1/Downloads/MeasureDocument/HB4076/Enrolled) on 2026-10-09. 469.401(3): a signed site certificate 'shall bind the state and all counties and cities and political subdivisions in this state as to the approval of the site', and they must issue the permits it addresses 'without hearings or other proceedings'. 469.504(1)(b) and (2): the Council may find goal compliance where the facility does not meet local substantive criteria, including by taking a goal exception. 469.401(5) keeps local authority over matters outside the certificate. Summary, state body and wind:300 (from 469.300(4) and (12)(a)(K)) match. Amendments confirmed: 469.401 history ends 2025 c.305; the 2026 table lists 469.504 amended by 2026 c.46 (HB 4076), which renumbers 469.504(2) into (2)(a) and adds (2)(b) deeming the exception standard met for a facility using an existing facility's surplus interconnection with no new transmission more than two miles out. That does not change the row; the citation 469.504(2) still points to the exception power.

summary: State land use rules cap solar PV on farmland that counties approve without a goal exception at 12 acres of high-value farmland, 20 acres of arable land and 320 acres of nonarable land, with a larger alternative path in eastern Oregon.
amendments_note: Rule history on the Secretary of State site: LCDD 5-2019 (eff. 2019-05-30, the rule Sabin describes), then LCDD 4-2021, LCDD 14-2024 (eff. 2025-01-01), LCDD 6-2025 (eff. 2026-01-01) and LCDD 10-2026 (eff. 2026-10-01). Section (44) lets eastern Oregon counties allow up to 160 acres on qualifying high-value farmland, 1,280 acres on arable land and 1,920 acres on non-arable land.
draft_note: Read the current rule text at secure.sos.state.or.us (2026-10-09). This is an administrative rule, not a statute (authority ORS 197.040). Larger projects need a Goal 3 exception under OAR 660-004 or a county program under OAR 660-023-0195. Sabin's '20 acres of other farmland' is the arable-land cap; nonarable land is 320 acres. The '86 percent of the Willamette Valley' figure is not in the rule.
review_note: Read OAR 660-033-0130 at https://secure.sos.state.or.us/oard/view.action?ruleNumber=660-033-0130 on 2026-10-09 (current text, history through LCDD 10-2026, effective 2026-10-01). (38)(g): solar PV on high-value farmland may not use more than 12 acres; (38)(i): arable land 20 acres; (38)(j): nonarable land 320 acres; (38)(k): an exception under ORS 197.732 and OAR 660 division 4 is needed to exceed them. (44): eastern Oregon counties may instead use (44)(b) to (n), with caps of 160 acres on qualifying high-value farmland, 1,280 acres on arable land and 1,920 acres on non-arable land ((44)(d)), or a program under OAR 660-023-0195. Summary, technology, local_government and state body (LCDC adopts the rule) match. One nuance the summary leaves out: (38)(h)(H) lets a facility exceed 12 acres on certain non-irrigated high-value farmland in a utility RPS service area without an exception. History matches the amendments_note for the period after June 2024 (LCDD 14-2024 eff. 2025-01-01, LCDD 6-2025 eff. 2026-01-01, LCDD 10-2026 eff. 2026-10-01); the note skips the 2020 amendments (LCDD 2-2020 to 15-2020), which predate the inventory and do not affect the row.

summary: The Energy Facility Siting Council certificates wind plants of 100 MW average capacity or more (300 MW peak under the 3.00 wind factor), solar thermal plants of 25 MW or more, and solar PV using more than 240, 2,560 or 3,840 acres depending on land class; counties handle smaller projects unless the developer or county elects state review.
amendments_note: The inventory's thresholds are out of date. 469.300 history: 2023 c.336; 2024 c.25 (HB 4015, battery storage); 2025 c.162 (HB 3874) raised the wind threshold from 50 to 100 MW average. Solar PV acreage is now 240/2,560/3,840 (inventory: 160/1,280/1,920). 2026 Or. Laws c.12 (HB 4031, eff. 91 days after 2026 sine die) amends 469.320 to exempt solar, wind, geothermal and marine facilities from the site certificate if local land use approval is applied for by 2028-12-31 and the project meets federal tax credit begin-construction and in-service conditions.
draft_note: Read ORS chapter 469 (2025 edition, oregonlegislature.gov), Oregon Laws 2025 c.162 and 2024 c.25 PDFs, enrolled 2026 HB 4031 (olis.oregonlegislature.gov) and the 2026 A&R table (469.320 by c.12; 469.504 by c.46). Threshold_mw shows 300 for wind because the statute counts 'average electric generating capacity' of 100 MW and 469.300(4) divides wind peak capacity by 3.00. Solar PV uses acreage, not MW, so it is not in threshold_mw. Battery storage is a related facility or an elective item under 469.320(8)(a)(C), not a stand-alone energy facility.
review_note: Read ORS chapter 469, 2025 edition, at https://www.oregonlegislature.gov/bills_laws/ors/ors469.html on 2026-10-09, plus Oregon Laws 2025 c.162 (https://www.oregonlegislature.gov/bills_laws/lawsstatutes/2025orLaw0162.pdf), the 2026 amended-and-repealed table (https://www.oregonlegislature.gov/bills_laws/lawsstatutes/2026OrLawAR.pdf) and enrolled 2026 HB 4031 (https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2026R1/Downloads/MeasureDocument/HB4031/Enrolled). 469.300(12)(a)(K): wind plant with 'average electric generating capacity of 100 megawatts or more'; 469.300(4): wind average capacity is peak divided by 3.00, so wind:300 MW peak is the right conversion. (12)(a)(A)(iii): solar thermal at 25 MW nominal. (12)(a)(D): solar PV using more than 240 acres of high-value farmland, 2,560 acres of cultivated or class I to IV land, or 3,840 acres of other land. 469.320(1) requires a site certificate; 469.320(8) lets the developer or the local government elect Council review for smaller wind, solar PV and battery storage. Summary, threshold and hybrid match. Amendments confirmed: 469.300 history ends 2023 c.336, 2024 c.25, 2025 c.162; c.162 struck wind from the 50 MW average clause and added the 100 MW wind clause. The 2026 table lists 469.320 amended by 2026 c.12 (HB 4031) and 469.300 not amended in 2026. HB 4031 adds 469.320(2)(h): solar, wind, geothermal or marine facilities need no site certificate if the developer applies for local land use approval by 2028-12-31 and receives it, notifies the local government and the Council that construction has begun for a federal 45, 45Y, 48 or 48E credit, and places the facility in service by 2030-12-31 (or a later date Treasury allows); effective the 91st day after the 2026 session adjourned, so in force now. The amendments_note describes this correctly; the drafter may want the summary itself to say that qualifying large projects can now go to the county instead.

summary: Pennsylvania has no state siting permit for wind or solar; municipalities (and counties where a municipality has no zoning) regulate them through zoning under the Municipalities Planning Code.
statute_citation: Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, Act of July 31, 1968, P.L. 805, No. 247, §§ 601, 602, 619 (53 P.S. §§ 10601, 10602, 10619)
amendments_note: The current compiled MPC on palegis.us shows a 2024 amendment (Act 44 of 2024, electronic transmittal, section 110) unrelated to energy siting; no 2024-2026 state wind or solar siting law found.
draft_note: Read the MPC PDF from palegis.us. Section 619 lets the PUC exempt a public utility corporation's buildings from zoning after a hearing; independent generators are not usually public utilities, so not drafted as preemption. No state statute names wind or solar siting.
review_note: Read the compiled Municipalities Planning Code PDF from palegis.us (https://www.palegis.us/statutes/unconsolidated/law-information/view-statute?txtType=PDF&SessYr=1968&ActNum=0247.&SessInd=0, linked from the statute_url page) on 2026-10-09. Section 601: each municipality's governing body may enact zoning ordinances; section 602: county zoning applies only in municipalities with no zoning ordinance in effect; section 619: the Public Utility Commission may exempt a public utility corporation's building from the zoning article after a hearing. The Code names solar and wind only as planning purposes, not as a state permit. Summary, technology and local_government fit; the 'no state siting permit' statement is an absence I could not disprove. state_body: Oficina de Gerencia de Permisos (OGPe), Department of Economic Development and Commerce
summary: Construction and land use permits, including for renewable projects, are issued by the central Permit Management Office (OGPe), except in autonomous municipalities holding a delegation of hierarchy levels I to V, which have exclusive permit authority under their delegation agreements.
statute_citation: Puerto Rico Act 161-2009 (Ley para la Reforma del Proceso de Permisos), art. 1.3 (23 L.P.R.A. § 9011 note); 23 L.P.R.A. § 9011 et seq.
amendments_note: OGPe's compiled text is marked 'Rev. 14 de mayo de 2026'; individual amendments not reviewed.
draft_note: Read the compiled Act 161-2009 PDF (Spanish) from bvirtualogp.pr.gov, article 1.3 (scope and autonomous municipalities' exclusive authority). The Act is a general permit law and does not single out wind or solar; Energy Bureau approvals under Act 57-2014 and Act 17-2019 were not read. Category is uncertain: OGPe is an agency, not a board, and delegated municipalities decide in their territory; the reviewer may prefer hybrid.
review_note: Read the compiled Act 161-2009 (Spanish, marked 'Rev. 14 de mayo de 2026') at https://bvirtualogp.pr.gov/ogp/Bvirtual/leyesreferencia/PDF/Permisos/161-2009.pdf on 2026-10-09: articles 1.3, 2.1, 2.5 and 18.10. Matches: art. 2.1 creates the Oficina de Gerencia de Permisos as an auxiliary secretariat of the Department of Economic Development and Commerce; art. 2.5 has OGPe (through its Junta Adjudicativa, permit managers and authorized professionals) issue final determinations and permits, including siting consultations; art. 1.3 gives autonomous municipalities with a delegation of hierarchies I to V 'total exclusividad para otorgar determinaciones finales y permisos' under their delegation agreements (also art. 18.10). The summary and citation match. Disagreement, field who_decides: the row says state_board, but the statute splits permit authority by place, with delegated autonomous municipalities deciding exclusively in their territory, as the row's own summary says; that is shared state and local authority (hybrid), not a state board alone. The drafter flagged this too. Also note: the Act is a general permit law and never mentions renewable, solar or wind projects, so 'including for renewable projects' is an application of the general rule, not statute text. Amendments: the compilation shows 2024-2025 changes by Laws 61-2024, 118-2024, 124-2024, 131-2024, 106-2025 and 111-2025 (arts. 2.7A, 3.4, 8.4, 8.4B, 8.16, 19.12); none changes arts. 1.3, 2.1, 2.5 or 18.10. Energy Bureau approvals under Acts 57-2014 and 17-2019 not read.

summary: For major energy facilities the Siting Board is the licensing authority for every permit or variance that state law or local ordinance would require; local boards hear the matter but only send findings and a recommendation to the Siting Board.
amendments_note: History ends with P.L. 1994, ch. 14; none shown as of 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read 42-98-7 on webserver.rilegislature.gov. DEM keeps federally delegated permits and CRMC keeps its coastal permits (42-98-7(a)(3)).
review_note: Read https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE42/42-98/42-98-7.htm on 2026-10-09. 42-98-7(a)(1) makes the Siting Board the licensing and permitting authority for every license, permit, assent or variance required by state statute or local ordinance; (a)(2) has the agencies and local boards that would otherwise decide 'sit and function at the direction of the siting board', follow their own procedures, and forward findings, the record and a recommendation to the Board instead of issuing the permit. (a)(3) keeps federally delegated DEM permits and DEM and CRMC permits with those agencies (the draft note says so). Summary, state body and the 40 MW threshold (42-98-3(e)) match. History ends with P.L. 1994, ch. 14; no change after June 2024 seen.

summary: Distributed generation projects in core forests (unfragmented blocks of 250 acres or more) are ineligible for the Renewable Energy Growth incentive program unless on a preferred site, and net-metering projects on adjoining parcels in core forests are not treated as distinct; the program's annual cap is up to 300 MW through 2033.
amendments_note: Enacted by P.L. 2023, ch. 300 and ch. 301 (2023-S 0684A, 2023-H 5853A), eff. 2023-06-24; 39-26.6-3 and 39-26.4-2 amended again by P.L. 2024, ch. 83 and ch. 84, eff. 2024-06-12 (contents of the 2024 change not compared).
draft_note: Read 39-26.6-3, 39-26.6-12 and 39-26.4-2 on webserver.rilegislature.gov. This is an incentive eligibility limit, not a siting ban: a project in a core forest can still be built without REG or net-metering benefits. On preferred sites in core forests no more than 100,000 sq. ft. of core forest may be cleared. The program covers all eligible renewables, though the core forest rule mainly affects solar.
review_note: Read on webserver.rilegislature.gov 2026-10-09: https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE39/39-26.6/39-26.6-3.htm, .../39-26.6/39-26.6-12.htm and .../TITLE39/39-26.4/39-26.4-2.htm. Confirmed: 39-26.6-3(6) defines core forest (250 acres or more, unbroken, 25 yards from mapped roads) and makes a distributed-generation project in a core forest ineligible for the Renewable Energy Growth program unless on a preferred site; (15) defines preferred sites; (7) caps core forest clearing at 100,000 sq. ft. on preferred sites; 39-26.6-12(c) sets annual targets 2023 through 2033 of up to 300 MW. Disagreements: (1) summary: the row says net-metering projects on adjoining core-forest parcels 'are not treated as distinct'; 39-26.4-2(19) says 'new and distinct projects cannot be located on adjoining parcels of land within core forests, except for preferred sites', subject to the safe harbor in 39-26.4-3(a)(1). The row's wording is an interpretation, and it drops the preferred-site exception. (2) amendments_note: it lists P.L. 2024, ch. 83 and 84 as the last change to 39-26.4-2, but the history note now also lists P.L. 2025, ch. 256 and ch. 269, both effective 2025-06-27. The current text still carries the core forest provisions, so the 2025 acts do not remove the rule, but the note should name them. 39-26.6-3 history ends with P.L. 2024, ch. 83 and 84 and 39-26.6-12 with P.L. 2023, ch. 300 and 301, as drafted.

summary: Generating facilities of 40 MW or more are major energy facilities licensed by the Energy Facility Siting Board; smaller facilities are regulated by city and town zoning.
amendments_note: None since the inventory: history notes on webserver.rilegislature.gov end with P.L. 2001, ch. 145 (42-98-3) and P.L. 1994, ch. 14 (42-98-7), as of 2026-10-09.
draft_note: Read 42-98-3 and 42-98-7 on webserver.rilegislature.gov. The inventory cites 42-98-3(d) for the threshold; the definition is now subsection (e). Storage is not named.
review_note: Read on webserver.rilegislature.gov 2026-10-09: https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE42/42-98/42-98-3.htm, .../42-98-7.htm and the chapter 42-98 index. 42-98-3(e): major energy facility includes 'facilities for the generation of electricity designed or capable of operating at a gross capacity of forty megawatts (40 MW) or more' (the definition is now subsection (e), as the draft says). 42-98-7(a)(1): the Siting Board is the licensing and permitting authority for all licenses, permits, assents or variances that state law or local ordinance would require for siting a major energy facility. Thresholds solar:40 and wind:40, state body and hybrid (Board at 40 MW and above, local zoning below) match; storage not named. History notes end with P.L. 2001, ch. 145 (42-98-3) and P.L. 1994, ch. 14 (42-98-7); the chapter index shows no new section, so no change after June 2024 seen.
